profile.title: Profile
profile.desc: Set your nickname and avatar; messages you send in conversations will use them.
profile.nicknameDesc: The name shown on messages you send in conversations.

pet.title: Desktop pet
pet.desc: Pick a companion to keep you company; it switches animations based on typing, thinking, tool execution and more.
pet.behaviorDesc: "Free" lets you drag it anywhere; "Perch on composer" only shows its head and front paws resting on the chat box.
pet.walk: Wander along the bottom when idle
pet.walkDesc: Strolls along the app's bottom edge after 10 minutes of inactivity, returning to the far right when there's activity.
pet.colorDesc: Pick a main color and the fur shades derive automatically; "Default" restores each design's original palette.

general.title: General
general.desc: Manage interface preferences, the default working directory and desktop behavior.
general.themeDesc: Light, dark or follow the system.
general.fontSizeDesc: Adjust the overall interface text size.
general.workspaceRootDesc: Where the agent runs for new project-less conversations / scheduled tasks without a project (leave empty to use the home directory).
general.openAtLoginDesc: Start Cortex automatically after you log in (macOS / Windows).
general.startMinimizedDesc: Minimize to the background after launch (mainly for Windows).
general.closeToTrayDesc: Hide to the system tray when the window is closed instead of quitting the app.
general.notesHotkeyDesc: Global hotkey to summon quick notes. Click and press a new combination to record; if it's taken you'll be notified and the old key kept.
general.notesHotkeyFailed: Failed to set hotkey; original hotkey kept
general.turnCompleteDesc: Show a system notification when an agent turn ends and the window is unfocused.
general.currentVersionDesc: Check for new versions available in GitHub Releases.
general.logEnabledDesc: Write main-process logs to a local file to help with troubleshooting.
general.logRetentionDesc: Old logs beyond the retention period are cleaned automatically on startup.

timeline.title: Timeline
timeline.desc: Configure the model that generates the AI daily report. Push channels are managed centrally in Push settings.
timeline.generateModeDesc: Integrated Agent uses the installed CLI; custom model uses an OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
timeline.providerDesc: The report runs on this provider (same source as a new Pi session).
timeline.piNoProvider: No enabled providers yet. Add and enable one in Providers settings first so Pi can generate reports.
timeline.baseUrlDesc: OpenAI-compatible API (Ollama / LM Studio / vLLM all work).

providers.title: Providers
providers.desc: Configure LLM providers (OpenAI-compatible / Anthropic-compatible endpoints). The Pi fallback agent uses providers here, selected in Agent settings; API keys are stored locally only.
providers.empty: No providers yet. Pick a template (or "Custom"), click "Add provider", fill in the API key, and you can use it in conversations.

models.customNoProbe: Custom endpoints don't support probing; add manually
models.hint: When a provider releases new models you can add them here manually or fetch from the API.
models.emptyHint: No models yet. Click "Add model" or "Fetch from API".

agent.title: Agent
agent.desc: Cortex supports three agents: Claude Code, Codex and the built-in Pi. Claude / Codex use their own CLI auth; Pi serves as a fallback when no CLI is installed, using the LLM endpoint configured in Providers. Pi's dedicated settings are in the Pi section.

pi.title: Pi
pi.desc: Pi is the built-in agent, running as a long-lived session. The settings below take effect on a new session or your next send; changing extension-type settings such as tool approval restarts the current pi session (losing in-memory context, auto-restored from on-disk history).
pi.noProvider: No enabled providers yet. Add and enable one in Providers settings first, then come back here to choose a default.
pi.defaultProviderDesc: The provider used by default for new Pi sessions.
pi.thinkingDefaultDesc: The default thinking level for new Pi sessions; each session can switch it separately next to the composer, taking effect instantly without restart.
pi.systemPromptDesc: Appended to the end of pi's system prompt to customize persona/rules. Changes take effect on your next send (restarts the current pi session).
pi.systemPromptPlaceholder: e.g. You are a senior TypeScript engineer; answer concisely and prioritize runnable code.
pi.toolApprovalDesc: Pi confirms via a dialog before calling high-risk tools; rejecting blocks the call. Changes take effect on your next send (restarts the current pi session, losing its in-memory context).
pi.approvalToolsDesc: Only checked tools trigger the confirmation dialog; unchecking all = approve no tools (equivalent to off).
pi.sampleToolsDesc: Loads the sample tool echo_upper (uppercases text) to demonstrate pi's custom tool capability. Changes take effect on your next send (restarts the session).
pi.sampleCommandsDesc: Loads the sample command /greet to demonstrate pi's custom slash command capability. Changes take effect on your next send (restarts the session).

push.title: Push channels
push.desc: Global push configuration; once enabled it can be used by any feature that supports push (such as the timeline daily report).
push.formatHint: Pin the push format with a .md template from the Prompt library; the first rendered line becomes the push title. Placeholders: {{placeholders}}; placeholder lines with empty data are hidden automatically.
push.exampleSkillDesc: Select a directory in the Prompt library on the right first.
push.dingtalkSecretDesc: Optional; fill in when the security setting is "Signature".
push.fromPlaceholder: Leave empty to use the account

voice.title: Voice (TTS)
voice.desc: Convert agent / LLM output into speech. With auto-read on, each turn is read aloud when it completes (code blocks and the like are skipped; a new reply interrupts the previous one).
voice.autoSpeakDesc: Read aloud when each turn completes (code blocks skipped; a new reply interrupts the previous one).
voice.voiceSystemDesc: Uses the local system voice library; no network or configuration needed.
voice.baseUrlDesc: OpenAI-compatible /v1/audio/speech (OpenAI TTS / LocalAI / Kokoro and other local deployments all work).
voice.testText: Hello, this is a voice test for Cortex Desktop.
